This vignette walks through a complete prediction workflow for one
calibration **pair** -- manta tow vs ReefScan Surface coral cover, at the
tow level -- using the package's three building blocks:

1. `rosetta_models()` to look up a model's fitting conventions,
2. a `pred*From*()` wrapper (or the generic `rosetta_predict()`) to turn a
   posterior-samples matrix into a prediction curve,
3. plotting the result.

RosettaGBR does not fit models or bundle posteriors (see `?RosettaGBR` /
the package README) -- every example below starts from a posterior-samples
matrix you supply. For a self-contained, always-reproducible vignette we
construct a **toy** posterior that mimics a real fit; the final section
shows how to swap in a real posterior from your own model fits instead.

```{r setup}
library(RosettaGBR)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 1. Look up the model

Every fitted model BR-04 produced is documented in the registry returned
by `rosetta_models()` -- one row per model, keyed by the same name as its
saved posterior file (`<model_name>.RDS`). Look up both directions of the
manta/RS-Surface coral-cover pair:

```{r}
rosetta_models() |>
  subset(model_name %in% c("manta_from_surf_tow", "surf_from_manta_tow")) |>
  subset(select = c(model_name, family, level, response_variable, predictor_variable, link))
```

Both directions are `"beta"` family (coral cover is a proportion) at
`"tow"` level, but as of 2026-10-15 they use *different* links (see the
registry's own `link` column above): `manta_from_surf_tow` is
`link = "loglog"` (`mu = exp(-exp(-eta))`) while `surf_from_manta_tow`
remains `link = "logit"` (`mu = plogis(eta)`), with no offset (coral cover
models have no effort term, unlike the COTS count models). You don't need
to branch on this by hand when calling `predBetaCurve()`, though -- it
reads the link straight off `attr(post, "link")` on whichever posterior
you pass it (defaulting to `"logit"` when that attribute is absent, so
every pre-existing posterior is unaffected), so the same function call
works for every Beta coral model regardless of which link it was fit
with. This tells us what each model's `x`/response actually are:

- **`manta_from_surf_tow`**: predicts manta tow `perc_hard` (response)
  from RS Surface `pct_HC_surf` (predictor).
- **`surf_from_manta_tow`**: the reverse direction -- predicts RS Surface
  `pct_HC_surf` from manta `perc_hard`.

Fitting a *separate* model per direction (rather than algebraically
inverting one fit) is deliberate: a Beta-regression fit of Y-on-X is not
the exact inverse of a fit of X-on-Y, so BR-04 fits and saves both
directions independently.

## 2. Obtain a posterior-samples matrix

Every `pred*From*()` function expects a matrix (or data frame) with one
row per posterior draw and, for a Beta-family model, columns `alpha`,
`beta`, `phi` -- this is the same contract
[RosettaCOTS](https://github.com/Scott-Foster/RosettaCOTS) uses, and
exactly what the BR-04 model fits were saved as (one `.RDS` file per model,
named `<model_name>.RDS`).

For this vignette we build a **toy** posterior with roughly the shape a
real fit might have (don't read anything into the specific numbers --
see Section 5 for how to load the real one):

```{r}
set.seed(4821)
post <- cbind(
  alpha = rnorm(4000, mean = -1.1, sd = 0.15),
  beta  = rnorm(4000, mean = 2.3,  sd = 0.20),
  phi   = rgamma(4000, shape = 12, rate = 1)
)
head(post)
```

## 3. Predict a calibration curve

Call the wrapper function named after the model (`manta_from_surf_tow` ->
`predMantaFromSurfTow()` -- see `?rosetta_models` / the README for the
naming convention), supplying the posterior and a grid of predictor
values:

```{r}
x_seq <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 100)
pred_manta <- predMantaFromSurfTow(post, x = x_seq)
pred_manta
```

The returned tibble has one row per `x` and five prediction columns:

- **`mean`** -- posterior mean of the fitted curve (population-level,
  group/random effects marginalized to zero).
- **`lo95`/`hi95`** -- 95% credible interval on that mean curve.
- **`pi_lo95`/`pi_hi95`** -- 95% *prediction* interval for a single new
  observation at that `x` (always at least as wide as the credible
  interval -- see `?predBetaCurve` for why this is enforced).

Equivalently, via the generic dispatcher (useful when looping over many
models by name rather than calling named functions one at a time):

```{r}
pred_manta2 <- rosetta_predict("manta_from_surf_tow", post, x = x_seq)
all.equal(pred_manta$mean, pred_manta2$mean)
```

## 4. Plot the calibration curve

```{r}
set.seed(99)
obs_x <- runif(60)
obs_mu <- plogis(-1.1 + 2.3 * obs_x)
obs <- data.frame(x = obs_x, y = rbeta(60, obs_mu * 10, (1 - obs_mu) * 10))

ggplot(pred_manta, aes(x, mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pi_lo95, ymax = pi_hi95), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = obs, aes(x, y), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(
    x = "RS Surface % hard coral (predictor)",
    y = "Manta tow % hard coral (predicted)",
    title = "predMantaFromSurfTow()",
    subtitle = "Mean (line), 95% credible interval (dark band), 95% prediction interval (light band)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

(`obs` above is simulated to roughly match the toy posterior, purely to
illustrate how you'd overlay real tow-level observations -- see Section 5
for the real data source.)

## 5. The other direction of the pair

The reverse-direction model, `surf_from_manta_tow`, has an *independent*
posterior (its own `alpha`/`beta`/`phi`) and predicts the opposite way --
RS Surface cover as a function of manta cover. Using a second toy
posterior (again, do not compare these specific numbers to the first --
they're just illustrative):

```{r}
set.seed(777)
post_rev <- cbind(
  alpha = rnorm(4000, mean = -0.9, sd = 0.18),
  beta  = rnorm(4000, mean = 1.9,  sd = 0.25),
  phi   = rgamma(4000, shape = 10, rate = 1)
)
pred_surf <- predSurfFromMantaTow(post_rev, x = x_seq)

ggplot(pred_surf, aes(x, mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pi_lo95, ymax = pi_hi95), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "darkorange", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Manta tow % hard coral (predictor)",
    y = "RS Surface % hard coral (predicted)",
    title = "predSurfFromMantaTow()"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 6. Using a real BR-04 posterior and real observations

The above uses toy posteriors so this vignette builds standalone, with no
dependency on files outside the package. If you have the saved BR-04
posterior and the corresponding tow-level data, swap them in instead:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Not evaluated when this vignette is built, since the package itself
# doesn't bundle this data. Adjust paths to wherever your files live.
post_real <- readRDS("path/to/manta_from_surf_tow.RDS")
tow_level <- readRDS("path/to/tow_level.RDS")

pred_real <- predMantaFromSurfTow(post_real, x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 100))

obs_real <- tow_level[!is.na(tow_level$pct_HC_surf) & !is.na(tow_level$perc_hard), ]

ggplot(pred_real, aes(x, mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pi_lo95, ymax = pi_hi95), fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = obs_real, aes(pct_HC_surf, perc_hard), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 1, alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "RS Surface % hard coral", y = "Manta tow % hard coral") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Note the real posterior matrix has extra columns beyond `alpha`/`beta`/
`phi` (per-reef random-effect draws, brms's internal `Intercept`/`lprior`/
`lp__`) -- every `pred*From*()` function selects columns by name, so these
extra columns are ignored automatically. `manta_from_surf_tow.RDS`
specifically also carries a `"link" = "loglog"` *attribute* (not a column)
on the saved matrix -- `attributes(post_real)` will show it -- which is
how `predMantaFromSurfTow()`/`predBetaCurve()` know to use the loglog
inverse link for this particular model without you passing anything extra.

  (family, level, offset/eps conventions, grouping, etc.).
- `?predBetaCurve` / `?predNegBinCurve` / `?predBinomialCurve` for the
